reason: E2 shows ML can predict hardness/strength in multi-phase alloys, supporting premise 1. E1 states that models using elastic constants, misfit volumes, and surface/USF energies can predict strengthening and ductility, supporting premise 2. However, neither E1 nor E2 provides evidence for extracting multilevel chemical fluctuation descriptors (premise 3), for the claimed efficiency gain of combining limited ab initio with microstructural data (premise 4), or for predicting fracture toughness via such an ML framework (premise 5).
premises: ML models can predict mechanical properties of multi-phase alloys with reasonable accuracy
Physics-based descriptors (elastic constants, misfit volumes, surface/USF energies) are sufficient to model strengthening and ductility in alloys
High-resolution microstructural descriptors can be extracted from SEM/TEM and nanoindentation
Combining limited ab initio descriptors with microstructural features reduces computational demand vs full DFT/CALPHAD
Fracture toughness can be predicted by the same integrated ML framework
